source.title: Adaptivity without Compromise: A Momentumized, Adaptive, Dual Averaged Gradient Method for Stochastic Optimization

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figures are represented by extracted text rather than page images; the experimental section also states the key test results in prose.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizers on held-out performance across image, language, and image-reconstruction tasks, using its own benchmarks and tuning procedure rather than reproducing the original comparisons exactly.
record.gate_note: The results compare optimizers using test-set metrics; training-loss metrics are shown alongside in Figures 3 and 4, but are not extracted as separate rows here. The paper also discusses weight-decay tuning, but reports no separate weight-decay outcome row beyond the optimizer results.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers' held-out performance with learning-rate and weight-decay sweeps and otherwise conventional settings. These results test V4; the study is not an original source. MRI reconstruction falls outside V4's image-classification and language scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record fairly summarizes the authors' conclusion: they present MADGRAD as a general-purpose optimizer combining strong empirical performance with convex convergence guarantees, including image-classification settings where Adam performs poorly. Their broad state-of-the-art characterization should remain attributed to them: Figure 4 reports better BookWiki test loss for AdaGrad than MADGRAD, and Section 7.5 contains conflicting numerical values.
record.recipe_differences: Compares a newly proposed adaptive method, Adam, AdaGrad, and SGD+M across several benchmarks; each method receives a learning-rate and decay sweep, with test performance used to select reported settings. It does not reproduce the Wilson et al. comparison exactly.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative performance varies by task: Adam and AdaGrad underperform SGD+M on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, while adaptive methods outperform SGD+M on fastMRI Knee, IWSLT14, or BookWiki. The paper recommends much lower weight decay for MADGRAD than typical SGD/Adam defaults; decay settings are swept by method.

fits_no_version.finding: On fastMRI reconstruction, Adam, AdaGrad, and MADGRAD have higher reported SSIM than SGD+M; MADGRAD also improves slightly over Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive optimizers can outperform momentum SGD on held-out MRI reconstruction quality.

record.problems: Only five seeds were used for the larger-scale problems; the paper says ImageNet preprocessing differs from He et al. (2016a), so test accuracy is not directly comparable to that setup. Results are selected by test-set performance after learning-rate and decay sweeps. Training-loss values are plotted but not separately extracted here.
record.rows_left_out: Training-loss values shown in Figures 3 and 4 were not extracted as separate rows; the test-set metrics directly measure the optimizer generalization comparison. No other separately stated qualifying results were omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting paired with natural-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local-connectivity interventions.

A controlled comparison of limited versus broader tuning, decoupled versus coupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and the specific word-level language-model exception. Weight decay is swept here, so these experiments are not an exact reproduction of learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning.
Dropout interventions, small-data regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

missing.what: Figure 1's additional CIFAR-10 adaptive-versus-SGD test-accuracy comparisons: SGD 94.26%, AdaGrad 91.31%, AdaGrad-DA 91.85%; stage-wise comparison SGD 94.33%, AdaGrad 92.05%, AdaGrad-DA 93.66%. These establish schedule-dependent magnitudes of the adaptive disadvantage.

The explicit observation that reducing weight decay improves MADGRAD on ImageNet but does not improve the other tested methods; the selected decay is 2.5e-5 for MADGRAD versus 1e-4 for the others. This qualifies the tuning conditions behind R8.

record.verdict_notes: Only the supplied text was used. All printed SE values are standard errors; error bars are twice those values. Hyperparameters were selected using test performance, so the reported held-out metrics are also tuning targets. Training-loss rows were explicitly declared omitted and are not listed as missing. Mixed optimizer and task outcomes qualify V4's scope rather than refuting its qualified 'often' formulation.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
Does not compare all adaptive optimizers or benchmark families in the version; does not test the effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD.

rows.subject: PreAct ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD+M; compared optimizer test performance.
rows.note: Reference non-adaptive optimizer result.
rows.check: Valid comparator, but SGD+M accuracy alone cannot establish an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage. The reported SE is 0.10 percentage points; plotted error bars represent twice the SE.

rows.subject: PreAct ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; compared optimizer test performance.
rows.note: Adam is below SGD+M on this image-classification task.
rows.check: Adam's 94.69% accuracy is below SGD+M's 95.22%; this fully exhibits the stated disadvantage, rather than a partial effect.

rows.subject: PreAct ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AdaGrad; compared optimizer test performance.
rows.note: AdaGrad is below SGD+M on this image-classification task.
rows.check: AdaGrad's 91.62% accuracy is below SGD+M's 95.22%; this fully exhibits the stated disadvantage.

rows.subject: PreAct ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Trained with MADGRAD; compared optimizer test performance.
rows.note: MADGRAD slightly exceeds SGD+M.
rows.check: MADGRAD reaches 95.38% versus SGD+M's 95.22%. This is the proposed method's result, but directly measures the adaptive-generalization comparison; the small numerical advantage should not be described as an established significant improvement.

relationships.condition: Adam and AdaGrad on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet, with learning-rate and weight-decay sweeps
relationships.reason: R2–R3 and R6–R7 show lower accuracy than SGD+M: 94.69/91.62 versus 95.22 on CIFAR-10 and 73.03/68.55 versus 76.09 on ImageNet.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower accuracies for Adam and AdaGrad than momentum SGD after hyperparameter sweeps remain unverified.

relationships.reason: R4 and R8 slightly exceed SGD+M, at 95.38 versus 95.22 and 76.22 versus 76.09, showing that the disadvantage does not extend to every adaptive optimizer.
relationships.display_finding: MADGRAD reportedly achieved slightly higher image-classification accuracy than momentum SGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.reason: R14–R16 show all adaptive methods below SGD+M's 4.49 test loss: Adam 4.35, AdaGrad 4.38, and MADGRAD 4.33.
relationships.display_finding: Adam, AdaGrad and MADGRAD reportedly achieved lower test loss than momentum SGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.reason: Figure 4's R18–R20 show lower test losses than SGD+M's 4.34: Adam 4.27, AdaGrad 4.06, and MADGRAD 4.20, despite conflicting numbers in Section 7.5.
relationships.display_finding: Reported results favor adaptive methods, but conflicting numerical accounts leave the comparison unverified.

relationships.condition: Additional CIFAR-10 AdaGrad comparisons without momentum, with flat or stage-wise schedules
relationships.reason: Missing rows in Figure 1 show AdaGrad and AdaGrad-DA below SGD: 91.31/91.85 versus 94.26 with flat adaptive schedules, and 92.05/93.66 versus 94.33 with stage-wise schedules.
relationships.display_finding: The reported accuracy deficits for AdaGrad and AdaGrad-DA under both schedule choices remain unverified.
